Your decisions before anything is built

There are 14 decisions and 17 new conventions (a new rule, style, icon or setting that needs your yes). Each one explains what happens today, what I propose, the other ways to do it, my recommendation and what else it touches. Everything applies to both the web app and the Android app unless it says otherwise.

Decision 1

Title sizes: popups, sheets and card heads

P1 popupsP2 card headsOpen

What happens today

The name of a popup is drawn in three sizes: the account popup and both wizards use 15 px, the "Code invoeren" sheet 17 px and the OwnifyAI question 22 px. Inside the account popup and the wizards, the first line of content (your username, "Wat wil je bijhouden?") is bigger than the popup's own name, so the order reads backwards.

Cards have the same problem. Overzicht and Gezondheid head their cards at 15 px, Community at 17 px. At 15 px a card's head is the same size as the items inside it, so nothing groups them. On the login, the "Wachtwoord vergeten?" link is almost as strong as the heading.

What I propose

One size for every popup and sheet title: 17 px semibold. That is the "Headline" step Ownify's type scale already assigns to a dialog's name. Card heads get the same 17 px. The items inside stay at 15, so the card groups them.

TodayAccountdev_jijLid sinds 4 jan 2026
ProposedAccountdev_jijLid sinds 4 jan 2026
Popup and sheet titles
Card heads

My recommendation

17 px for both. Ownify's type scale already says that a dialog's name and a card's name are Headline 17. Community already shows it works, and it gives every screen a clear title, then content, then action. Combined with decision 3, the login then reads: title → fields → green "Inloggen" → a quiet "Wachtwoord vergeten?".

What else it touches

  • Every popup, wizard and sheet, and about 35 card heads, on both apps.
  • A long card head next to its icon may wrap on a small (320 px) phone. I'll check that in the prototype.
  • The design document's type table gets corrected: it describes card titles at a size the app doesn't use.
  • On the login and "forgot password" screens, only one title will show (today there are two).

Decision 2

Delete, wipe and leave: one rule

P1Open

What happens today

Actions that destroy something have five different looks, and how loud they look is the reverse of what's at stake:

  • Gegevens wissen (your health data goes, the account stays) is the loudest: raised gold glass.
  • Account verwijderen (everything goes) is the quietest: a small grey underlined link.
  • Vriend verwijderen, Uitdaging verlaten and Ontkoppelen are tiny 11 px text.
  • Doel verwijderen looks exactly like Pauzeren.

In "Je gegevens" (your example 5), the safe "Downloaden" is a flat button while both "Wissen" buttons float in gold, so they read as the main actions. The row labels are dimmed like the disabled switches above them, and the buttons are 36 px tall where everything else is 44.

What I propose

One rule on both apps. The button that starts a destructive action is the normal button with a bin icon; it only asks the question. The final, irreversible "yes" is the gold glass. The question always appears the same way: a gold-edged note in place, as the goal page does today. All of these buttons are 44 px tall, and the row labels use normal ink.

Option A · neutral first, gold to confirm
Gegevens wissen
tap ↓

Je metingen, scores en doelen worden gewist. Dit kan niet ongedaan worden gemaakt.

Option B · gold everywhere
Gegevens wissen
Account verwijderen
dev_lisa

Then the confirm is gold as well.

The rule for destructive actions

My recommendation

A. If gold is kept for the moment that really can't be undone, it keeps its meaning. With B, a card like "Je gegevens" has three gold buttons outshining the safe "Downloaden", and the friend list turns into a column of gold. A also matches what the goal page already does. Whichever you choose, "Account verwijderen" will no longer be quieter than "Gegevens wissen".

What else it touches

  • Privacy (Je gegevens), Account verwijderen, the friends list, challenges, devices (Ontkoppelen), goals, trainings and deleting OwnifyAI chats, on both apps.
  • One sentence in the design document changes. That is new convention N2 below.
  • The friend row needs a little more room for a full-size button.
  • What each action does, and what the server does, stays exactly the same.

Decision 3

Button text sizes

P2Open

What happens today

The green "Volgende" in the wizards has 15 px text. The green "Toestaan en beginnen" and every normal button have 13 px. "Verwijderen" and "Uitdaging verlaten" are 11 px. One look, three sizes, and the design document doesn't say which is right. On the login, the 13 px button is weaker than the heading above it.

Proposed
dev_jij

Full-width and green buttons 15 · a button beside a field 13 · nothing at 11.

Button text sizes

My recommendation

15 for main buttons and 13 beside a field. The one action a screen leads to should be the clearest thing on it, and 15 px is what the green "Volgende" already uses. Buttons next to a field stay compact so the field keeps its width. Nothing important should ever be fine print.

What else it touches

  • Every button on both apps. The rule gets written into the design document, which says nothing about button text today.
  • I'll check the small-phone width for buttons that sit beside a field.

Decision 4

The account popup and your profile

P1 photoP2 the restOpen

What happens today

Decision 6

Privacy and consent wording

P2Open

What happens today

In Privacy, the OwnifyAI block names Gemini four times and says "turning it on is consent" twice (in the intro and on the switch). A usage tip ("veeg omhoog") sits in a privacy section. In Account › Lichaamsmaten, the same fact about keeping your history is written twice on one screen.

Related: under "Later instelbaar", two switches are shown switched on but can't be changed. "Profiel vindbaar" already works through friend search, and "Vriendverzoeken toestaan" lives in the account popup instead of Privacy.

My draft (Dutch; I'll add the English)

Intro: "OwnifyAI is gemaakt met Google Gemini, via de gratis Gemini API. Google kan wat binnenkomt gebruiken om zijn producten te verbeteren, en medewerkers van Google kunnen het lezen."

Then: the switch "Gegevens verwerken met Google Gemini" with its short state note. The separate info block goes. The sentence about keeping chats until you wipe them moves to the "OwnifyAI-gesprekken wissen" row, where it belongs. The swipe tip leaves Privacy.

The OwnifyAI consent text
The "Later instelbaar" switches

My recommendation

Start from the draft. Repetition buries the one sentence that matters: that Google may use and read what goes in. Because this is consent text, you approve the final words.

What else it touches

  • The Privacy page and the OwnifyAI consent popup on both apps, and the English translations.
  • How OwnifyAI handles data doesn't change, only the words.

Decision 7

Icons: one meaning per icon

P1 four conflictsP2 the restOpen

What happens today

Both apps use exactly the same icon set, which is good. But several icons mean two or more things, so they can't teach you anything. The icons with a gold edge below are the conflicts.

Moon

Slaap and Thema & uiterlijk.

Chart

The Doelen tab and every Verloop on the other tabs.

Pulse

Heart rate, sleep insights, Gezondheidsscore, active minutes.

Info

A tip, an error, Over de app, Voorwaarden.

Lock

"No data yet" (reads as "forbidden"), private, locked.

Copy

Copying a code and Licenties.

Chevron down

Close a sheet and open a list, in the same sheet.

Bolt

Activiteit, Stappen, Energie and training insights (Training is the dumbbell elsewhere).

Plus / person-plus

"Vriend toevoegen" uses both, in four different looks.

What I propose, using only existing icons

  • Insights take their category's icon (Slaap , Training ). Pulse is only for heart rate.
  • Licenties gets Info, like Voorwaarden. Copy is only for copying.
  • Every "add a friend" uses person-plus (). Plus is only for creating something.
  • Bolt is only for Activiteit. "No data yet" loses the lock. Thema no longer uses the moon.
  • Errors no longer use Info (see the question about new icons).
  • The Doelen tab keeps the chart. The Verloop cards get the tile of their own category.
Re-map the icons as above?
May I add two new icons?
The close button of sheets

My recommendation

Re-map everything and allow the two new icons. An icon only helps when it always means the same thing. An error shown with the "info" icon tells you it's harmless. The two new icons are small and match the existing family.

What else it touches

  • Both apps at once: the Android icons are generated from the web set.
  • Every Verloop card head, the insights, Instellingen rows, error notes, friend buttons and the sheets' close button.

Decision 8

Charts: one set of conventions

P1 four errorsP2 the restOpen

What happens today

The charts follow Ownify's chart standard for their time windows, but several details go wrong:

Also: the dots come in four policies, three sizes and three side margins. Voeding and Training are hard to tell apart for colour-blind people, and some lines are faint in Dark Mode. SpO₂ going from 96 to 98 % fills the whole chart, so it looks like a big swing.

The proposal, item by item (tick what you approve)

My recommendation

Approve all eleven as one package. Items 1–6 fix things that are wrong today. Items 7–11 make every chart follow one set of rules, so a dot, a key or a date always looks and behaves the same. I'll add the new rules to the chart standard, so future charts follow them too.

What else it touches

  • Every chart over time on both apps: Verloop, Gezondheidsscore, area charts, heart rate and goals.
  • The chart standard document and its tests are updated.
  • No calculation changes, only how things are drawn.
  • I couldn't judge the 30-, 90- and 365-day score shapes, because the test data has only two days of scores. That comes back in the new screenshots.

Decision 9

The back gesture

P1 webP2 AndroidOpen

What happens today

Web: on a phone, the system back gesture (Android) or the left-edge swipe (iPhone Safari) leaves Ownify, or goes back to the previous website, instead of closing the page or popup you have open. The most common "go back" does the most destructive thing.

Gezondheid→Slaap detail open→ back →You've left Ownify

Android app: back closes details and popups correctly. But on any tab other than Overzicht, back closes the app instead of returning to Overzicht.

What I propose

Gezondheid→Slaap open→ back →Gezondheid→ back →Overzicht→ back →leave

On the web, each open layer (a detail, a popup, a sheet) adds one step to the browser's history, so back closes the top layer. On Android, back on another tab first goes to Overzicht.

Web
Android

My recommendation

Both. A back gesture that throws you out of the app is the single biggest "this is a website" moment left. The Android change is small and matches what Android users expect.

What else it touches

  • Every detail page, popup, wizard, the devices panel and the OwnifyAI sheet on the web.
  • Care is needed so the back pill and the back gesture never close two layers at once, and so a reload doesn't reopen an old state.
  • Needs a check on a real iPhone and Android phone.

Decision 10

The Overzicht arrival animation

P2Open

What happens today

Every time Overzicht opens, the score counts up for 2.5 seconds and the ring settles at about 3.5 seconds. Only then do the three pillar rings start, finishing at about 5.2 seconds. It can't be skipped, and it's the screen you see most.

0 s12345 s
Score counts2.5 s
Ring settles3.5 s
Pillar rings5.2 s
Proposed: all≈1.5 s
The arrival

My recommendation

Shorter. The more often you see an animation, the shorter it should be. This one stands between you and your score several times a day. At about 1.5 seconds it still feels like Ownify's ring arriving, without making you wait.

What else it touches

  • Overzicht on both apps. "Animaties uit" keeps showing it instantly.
  • The timing gets a final check with the motion review skill, which only you can start.

Decision 13

Leftovers I'm not sure about

P3Open

What happens today

The cleanup phase removes code nobody uses. For most of it I'm certain. These six I'm not, because they could be meant for later or used outside what I can see.

A "connection status" check for the Android app

The documentation says the app should call it at startup, but no version of the app ever has. Only test tools use it.

The "badges" card on Community

A placeholder that is never shown. Its text is still sent to the Android app on every load.

"Suggest a target" for challenges

Added in 49.1 and unused since challenges let the group choose its own number (49.3–49.5).

A "computed, not editable" style for settings

Settings support a field that is worked out by the app and can't be edited, but no setting uses it today.

Two unused hooks in the pull-to-sync script

They're labelled "for the browser tests", but no such test exists in the project.

The local test database "g7"

It is missing three database updates (the e-mail accounts, research and insights updates), so tests run on it don't match the live app. It's local only.

My recommendation

As marked: remove what nobody uses, keep the one small option a future setting could need, and update the test database so tests reflect the live app.

What else it touches

  • None of these are visible in the app. Removing the badges text makes the data the Android app downloads slightly smaller.

Decision 14

Android refresh and server speed settings

P2Open

What happens today

Every time the Android app comes back to the front, and after every change you make, it downloads the whole app state again: about 486 KB. A quarter of that is text that never changes (licences, research). The web serves its 17 style files and 33 script files without settings for compression or long-term caching in the project, so every visit may load them again. I couldn't see the live server's own settings.

Today486 KB
Compressed95 KB
Turn on compression on the server
Let browsers keep the style and script files
How often Android refreshes when you return to it

My recommendation

All three. Compression and caching are pure speed with no visible change, and the one-minute rule removes needless reloads while keeping the data fresh. I'll measure before and after in the performance phase.

What else it touches

  • Compression and caching are server settings that reach the live site through a normal release, so they need your approval to ship.
  • The refresh rule changes when the Android app reloads, not what it shows.
  • No new costs or services.

Approval list

The 17 new conventions

Ownify's rule is that nothing new (a style, rule, token, icon or way of working) gets added without your yes. Several decisions above lead to one of these, which is noted on each. Approving a decision's option and approving its convention go together; you can still say "discuss" here.

When you're done

Export your decisions and send me the file in our chat, or copy them as text and paste it. Then I start Phase 3: prototypes of the approved changes for you to see before anything is built.
